_doc: Per-page metadata for the Category-15 (Feminine Care) standard renderer (tools/build-category-standard-pages.mjs). Numbers come from data/standards/cat15-compiled/<record>.json (frozen derivations from the index repo's deterministic compiler, tools/standards/compile-cat15.mjs); nothing numeric is authored here. The category splits into two instrument families in the same mucosal basis: DEVICE forms (no per-metal numeric content limit → every cell a mandatory control or substantiated not-material) and COSMETIC forms (sovereign mucosal-contact cosmetic limits apply).

_meta.method_label: Sovereign mucosal-contact cosmetic ML (cosmetic forms); read-across by analogy (device forms)
_meta.methodology_version: Method v2.0 — government-limit default, mucosal basis (CLAUDE.md Part 19)
method_prose: Feminine-care products contact the vulvovaginal mucosa, which is markedly more permeable and bioavailable than intact skin; the standard is written on a mucosal basis and never on a dermal or dietary basis. The category splits into two instrument families that share this basis but are never conflated. Device forms — tampons, pads, cups, discs, period underwear — are regulated as medical devices for biocompatibility (21 CFR Part 884; EU MDR 2017/745; ISO 10993), but no government sets a per-metal numeric content limit for a menstrual product.

Rather than leave those cells blank, the standard reads a limit across by analogy: for each analyte it adopts the strictest health-based limit a government has set for an article in comparable prolonged mucosal contact, and holds the device to that number. The read-across is disclosed and deliberately conservative, so every device cell is a read-across to a named government limit and never a number HMTc originated, with inorganic arsenic and methylmercury bounded by their parent totals and measured every lot.

Cosmetic forms — feminine wipes, deodorants, douches, intimate washes — are cosmetics, so sovereign cosmetic contaminant limits apply, adopted at the strictest mucosal-contact tier a government draws. Lead reads across the German BVL 2017 toothpaste tier (500 µg/kg, stricter than the general-cosmetic 2000 because vaginal mucosa is more permeable than the oral mucosa that limit was written for); cadmium (100), total arsenic (500) and total mercury (100) bind the strictest general-cosmetic value directly; and nickel binds the only sovereign cosmetic nickel content limit (Korea MFDS 2025, 10000). Occurrence establishes materiality — a metal a routed survey measures present cannot be recorded not-material — but never sets the number.
_meta.derivation_lead: For {name}, each HMTc limit is a disclosed read-across to the strictest health-based limit a government sets for a comparable mucosal-contact article, named in the Binding column. Cosmetic forms bind a cosmetic limit that applies to the product directly; device forms, for which no government sets a per-metal numeric content limit, carry the same value by read-across by analogy. Inorganic arsenic and methylmercury are bounded by their parent totals, and no number is originated by HMTc.

pages.name: Menstrual tampons
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified heavy-metal-safety standard for menstrual tampons (Feminine Care), evaluated on the total heavy-metal content of the finished article as placed on market (mucosal basis; the applicator is tested as a distinct component). No government sets a per-metal numeric content limit for this menstrual product, so every analyte is held to a disclosed read-across by analogy, the strictest health-based limit a government sets for an article in comparable prolonged mucosal contact, with inorganic arsenic and methylmercury bounded by their parent totals.
